rows.08:6ca0:
"Oh, it's been a while."
It was a classmate.
"M-Mayuko☆
Wh-what happened to you★"
No wonder she was shocked. There was no trace left of how Mayuko used to look, and the girl couldn't help looking away.{p}
rows.08:6d5c:
"I wanted to see everyone...
I'm so lonely."
Looking at just the hand she held out, the nails were cracked and white, the skin blotched and wrinkled. It looked nothing like the hand of a seventeen-year-old.
"What lovely hair. Let me touch it..."
And what do you think she did?
She tore her classmate's hair off, scalp and all, and gently set it on her own head.
"Isn't my hair lovely?
Hee hee.
Oh, what's wrong?
You don't have any hair.
You poor thing.
I know☆
I've just had the most wonderful idea!"{p}
rows.08:7000:
They say Mayuko disappeared without a trace after that.
Later, so many students got burned at that incinerator that it was declared dangerous, and now they say only the janitor goes near it.
There's certainly a spiritual chill hanging in the air there.
Maybe the earthbound spirit has many other victims, too.
That's the end of my story.
Who's next?{p}
rows.08:714c:
"Oh, it's been a while."
It was a classmate.
"Aaagh, a monsterrr☆"
No wonder he was shocked.
There was no trace left of how she used to look, and his legs gave out under him.
He didn't even have the courage to look up.
"C-could you be... Mayuko...?"
This boy used to follow her around constantly, fawning over her at every opportunity.{p}
rows.08:7284:
"That's a rather cruel thing to say..."
Looking at just the hand she held out, the nails were cracked and white, the skin blotched and wrinkled. It looked nothing like the hand of a seventeen-year-old.
"You've got nice, sturdy bones, haven't you?"
Then she breathed her rank, fishy breath into his face.
He was so terrified that he fainted.{p}
rows.08:739c:
She grabbed the boy, who had fainted from the shock, by the legs and threw him into the incinerator right beside them, still blazing hot!
"Gyaaaaaaaargh☆"
Before the scream had even died away, she shut the door.
After about an hour, I suppose, she opened the incinerator door and raked out the ashes with a stick.
Then she gathered up the bones, still hot, and slowly began stuffing her cheeks with them, munching away.
"Bones. More bones...
Hee hee hee.
Now my illness will be cured.
I can be pretty again, just like I used to be."
Mayuko couldn't help doing a little dance of joy.{p}
rows.08:75b0:
They say she disappeared without a trace after that.
Later, so many students got burned at that incinerator that it was declared dangerous, and now they say only the janitor goes near it.
{a}{f:,|,} there really is an earthbound spirit there, you know.
Well, that's the end of my story.
Who's next?{p}
rows.08:76cc:
Yes, the bronze statue was part of it too.
At first, anyway...
But that spot was far too inconspicuous for a statue, so they moved it next to the school gate.
You see it every day on your way to school, don't you?{p}So, there's something they built there after that.
rows.08:77c4:
That's right, the gym.
There are all sorts of rumors about that place.
For example... let's see.
Shall I tell you about Koji Oyama, who was in the basketball club?{p}
rows.08:7868:
He was quiet and didn't stand out, but he had more passion for basketball than anyone.
But he never won a starting spot, never even made the bench, and was stuck fetching balls alongside the younger students.
Students like that often quit the club, but he stuck with it and kept working hard as a member of the basketball club.
After the starters and the reserves finished practice, he would stay and practice alone until late at night.
Even if Oyama could never be a starter, he was happy just being able to play basketball.
But one day, his practicing alone so late became a problem.
He was forbidden to use the gym alone late at night.
Oyama was sad, but he thought the teacher had a fair point.{p}
rows.08:7afc:
After that, for a while, he practiced in the park or out on the street.
Then, about ten days later...{p}
rows.08:7b68:
On his way home from the park, as he passed in front of the school, he heard a ball bouncing in the gym.
It was already past eleven.
Oyama thought it was strange, so he went onto the school grounds and headed for the gym.
There was no light in the gym's windows; it was far too dark for club practice.{p}
rows.08:7c48:
He couldn't hear anything anymore, and he was about to go home when he heard the ball bouncing again.
"Who could be practicing in a pitch-dark gym...?"
The thought made him so envious he couldn't stand it, they say.
Unable to hold himself back, he went into the gym.{p}
rows.08:7d44:
Inside it was pitch dark, and the sound had stopped.
"Hey! Is anybody there?"
"Let me practice with you too!"
Everything was silent, and no one answered.
Just as Oyama gave up and turned to go home, shadowy figures began to loom faintly out of the dark at the far end.{p}
rows.08:7e3c:
When he crept closer, he saw four students standing there in basketball uniforms.
(I've never seen these guys before.)
rows.08:7ebc:
Oyama thought to himself.
"You guys aren't in the basketball club, are you?"
When Oyama said that, they answered.
"Wanna play with us? But you have to keep it a secret."
Oyama hesitated.
But it had been days since he was banned from practicing at night, and he was dying to have a proper practice.
"Okay, sure."
With that, Oyama started practicing basketball with them.
After a while, one of them spoke.
"Will you come tomorrow too?"
This time Oyama answered without hesitating.
"Can I?"
"But you can't tell anyone. It's a secret."
With that, the four of them vanished toward the far side of the gym.{p}
rows.08:80e8:
The next day, Oyama could hardly wait for night to come.
That night, when he went to the gym as promised, they were waiting for him.
"We've been waiting for you."
One of them said that, and the five of them started practicing basketball again.
That went on every night for more than ten days.
One night, as Oyama was about to go out again, his parents caught him, and he couldn't go to practice.
But in the middle of the night, Oyama snuck out and went to the gym anyway.{p}
rows.08:8280:
"We thought you weren't coming tonight."
They said it with big smiles.
"I might not be able to come anymore."
When Oyama said that, they answered.
rows.08:8324:
"Why? Are you sick of practicing with us?"
He flatly denied it.
"No, that's not it.
My parents got mad at me for staying out so late at night.
Honestly, I'd love to keep practicing with you guys forever."
"Then come."
"But I can't anymore.
Sorry. It's been fun up till now."
The four of them said as they drew closer,
"No, you have to come every day."
"No way. We're not letting you go hooome."
They surrounded Oyama.
"Let's play basketball together."{p}
rows.08:84e4:
Oyama has been missing ever since.
But they say if you go to the gym at night, you'll find five of them practicing basketball.
Now they have a full team of five.
And I hear they're looking for a team to play against next.
That's why, in the basketball club, it's quietly said that five people must never practice together at night.
When I heard this story, I thought right away that it was the earthbound spirit's doing.
At this school, lots of people use the gym without knowing about the spirit lurking there.
{a}{f:,|,} you'd better be careful too.
Well, that's the end of my story.
Who's next?{p}
rows.08:87e0:
Grind, grind, crunch! A dull sound echoed through the gym as his arm was dragged in deeper and deeper.
The only way to pull his arm free would have been to tear it off, and from the pain and the panic, he passed out.{p}
rows.08:88b4:
What happened to him?
Luckily, his teammates came to check on him and found him, so his life was saved, but...
His arm was amputated at the right shoulder, and he spent a long time in the hospital.
In the end, he couldn't even go to cheer at his last game.
He fell into a deep depression, and on the night of the gym's opening ceremony, he killed himself on the spot where he'd lost his arm.
rows.08:89d0:
Cursing his own misfortune.
If only he hadn't put his hand into that concrete mixer...{p}
rows.08:8a34:
He must have been so sad. They say that when he killed himself, a mannequin's arm, brought from who knows where, was tied to his shoulder with string.
Oh yes, that reminds me. The beginning of August the school nurse mentioned... isn't that when the summer high school baseball tournament is held?
And the injured students all belong to the same club: the baseball club.
And it's always their dominant arm, too...{p}
rows.08:8b74:
...{a}{f:,|,} the gym is dangerous.
I've heard all sorts of other stories about it, too.
Well, let's save those for another time.
That's the end of my story.
Who's next?{p}
rows.08:8c30:
She was overjoyed.
She was happier than she probably would have been even if her own illness were cured.
She was so happy that all the gardening club members were tormented with guilt.
But from what they'd heard, her condition was quite serious, and if her illness really couldn't be cured, they felt it might be kinder not to tell her...
They all forced themselves to smile.
"The flowers are doing great. Even on rainy days like this, they're all in bloom.
Isn't that amazing?
Right now, those hydrangeas you love are in full bloom.
Let's see... It'd be nice if you could leave the hospital by the time the sunflowers you planted bloom, Hayasaka.
So hurry up and get well.
It's lonely without our 'Guardian of the Flower Bed.'"
After all her visitors had gone home, she thought quietly to herself.
(I know my own body well. Better than the doctors do.
The truth is, I don't have much longer...)
The more she thought about it, the more her thoughts turned to the flowers in the flower bed.
If she was never going to leave this place again, she wanted to take care of the flowers one last time.
And to say goodbye to them...{p}
rows.08:8fdc:
And so she headed for the school.
Even though she could barely get out of bed.
Outside, the soundless rain peculiar to the rainy season was falling.
It was a chilly day, not the usual rainy-season chill, but a cold that went right to the bone.
Even though the rainy season was almost over...
At the school flower bed, she stood frozen.{p}
rows.08:9110:
"The flowers have withered☆
Why★
You mean everyone was lying to me★
Uhh... I'm sorry. If I hadn't gotten sick, you wouldn't have withered like this.
...I'll make you all better right now."
Forgetting that she was ill herself, she tended the flowers for hours.{p}
rows.08:933c:
"I'm glad you're better.
Look, even the flowers seem happy that you're well again, Hayasaka."
"Hee hee, do you think so?
I suppose they really did feel my heart.
Or perhaps... hee hee hee."
"What is it?"
"Hee hee hee hee. They've all grown so lively for me. I'm so happy.
For these little ones, I could do anything.
Anything at all..."{p}
rows.08:9490:
As she said that, for some reason she seemed cold, like a different person.
I hear her family runs a private obstetrics and gynecology clinic, and apparently she fed aborted babies to the flowers as fertilizer...{p}
rows.08:9558: Well, when you think about it, what actually becomes of the children who are disposed of in the dark without ever being born into this world... that's something we can't even imagine.{p}
rows.08:96d8:
Is that a bit too convenient an interpretation?
Yes, but I can't help thinking so.{p}
rows.08:9740:
How do I know this story?
The gardening club member who heard her say that was my older brother.
Of course, nothing bad happens at that flower bed now.
What worries me is that someday, someone might go in there just to make mischief.
And trample the flowers Hayasaka raised with such care...
If that happens... I won't be responsible for whatever happens to them.
After all, they'll have brought it on themselves.
Oh, and come to think of it, there's one more strange thing...
Do you know what 'perennials' and 'annuals' are?
A perennial is a plant whose roots survive even when it withers for the year, so the same plant grows in the same spot the next year. An annual is a plant that, once it withers, has to be grown again from seed.
Except for the hydrangeas, all the flowers Hayasaka grew were annuals. But strangely, the same flowers bloom there every year without anyone planting seeds.
Look, you can see them from the window, can't you?
Those huge sunflowers...
Well, that's the end of my story.
Who's next?{p}
rows.08:9ab8:
Yes. Perhaps her feelings got through to them, because the flowers didn't wither; they kept growing strong.
Or was it because the other gardening members were caring for the flowers with all their might, even if they weren't quite as good at it as she was?
Truly, even though it was still the rainy season, the flowers were blooming in every color.
Normally, when it rains, flowers don't open much, and even when they do, their colors aren't vivid. But her flower bed was magnificent, far beyond anything common sense would allow.
In a season that's dreary and depressing enough as it is, you could see that it put everyone's hearts at ease.{p}
rows.08:9ce4:
Unlike the flowers, though, her condition was not improving.
When the gardening club members she was close to went to visit her,
"Are they all doing well?
They aren't wilting, are they?"
That's what she asked them.{p}
rows.08:9d9c:
She was more worried about the flowers than about her own body, so whatever they talked about, the conversation always ended up on the school flower bed.
"The flowers are doing great. Even on rainy days like this, they're all in bloom.
Isn't that amazing?
Right now, those hydrangeas you love are in full bloom.
Let's see... It'd be nice if you could leave the hospital by the time the sunflowers you planted bloom, Hayasaka.
So hurry up and get well.
It's lonely without our 'Guardian of the Flower Bed.'"
After all her visitors had gone home, she thought quietly to herself.
"I know my own body well.
Better than the doctors do.
The truth is, I don't have much longer..."
The more she thought about it, the more her thoughts turned to the flowers in the flower bed.
If she was never going to leave this place again, she wanted to take care of the flowers one last time.
And to say goodbye to them...{p}
rows.08:a050:
She hurried to the school.
She could barely even get out of bed.
Outside, the soundless rain peculiar to the rainy season was falling.
It was a chilly day, not the usual rainy-season chill, but a cold that went right to the bone.
Even though the rainy season was almost over...{p}
rows.08:a1cc:
The next day, when the gardening club member on duty came to the flower bed to tend the flowers as usual, a hospital slipper was lying on the ground.
Thinking 'It can't be,' he searched the area, but she wasn't there.
Then he glanced down and noticed something odd about the base of the sunflower at his feet.
And he froze in horror.
A single finger was poking out of the soil at its roots.{p}
rows.08:a324:
He dug frantically, and there she lay, already cold, with a satisfied smile on her face.
And they say the fine rootlets of every plant in the flower bed had latched onto her pores, as if they were growing out of her.{p}
rows.08:a41c:
How do I know this story?
The gardening club member who found Hayasaka in the flower bed was my older brother.
I heard this story from him.
He says he often tended the flowers together with her.
And after she went into the hospital, he was the one who worked so hard to look after them in her place.
My brother said it must have been the earthbound spirit haunting that place that dragged her under.
At first, I thought so too.{p}
rows.08:a5b0:
But now I think that might not be quite right.
Maybe it was what she wanted...
She knew for herself how little time she had left, after all.
So if she was going to die anyway, didn't she truly wish to become nourishment for those flowers?
I believe that strong wish and something spiritual worked together, and that's how it ended up that way.{p}
rows.08:a718:
Of course, nothing bad happens at that flower bed now.
What worries me is that someday, someone might go in there just to make mischief.
And trample the flowers Hayasaka raised with such care.
If that happens... I won't be responsible for whatever happens to them.
After all, they'll have brought it on themselves.
Oh, and come to think of it, there's one more strange thing...
Do you know what 'perennials' and 'annuals' are?
A perennial is a plant whose roots survive even when it withers for the year, so the same plant grows in the same spot the next year. An annual is a plant that, once it withers, has to be grown again from seed...
Except for the hydrangeas, all the flowers Hayasaka grew were annuals. But strangely, the same flowers bloom there every year without anyone planting seeds.
Look, you can see them from the window, can't you?
Those huge sunflowers...
Well, that's the end of my story.
Who's next?{p}
rows.08:aa34:
Yes, they called in a Buddhist priest.
Even though it was a scorching summer day, all the senior teachers gathered in formal black clothes, holding prayer beads.
That's how serious they all were.
All the students knew was their friends' experiences and rumors, but the teachers had read the records of every strange incident since the school was founded.
Rumor has it the records even say what made the earthbound spirit start appearing.
I don't know the details about that.
If you're interested, why not look into it?
It'd make quite a scoop.
All I know about is what happened during that exorcism.{p}
rows.08:ac68:
On the day of the exorcism, the priest didn't show up, even after the scheduled time had passed.
The teachers talked it over and decided that one of them would wait for the priest at the main gate, while the rest would wait at the spot in question.
It happened a little while after everyone had gathered there.
Mr. Iida, a newly hired teacher, started saying something like this.{p}
rows.08:ad88:
"This is ridiculous. Is there really such a thing as an earthbound spirit?"
Mr. Iida seemed to have other plans, and he was getting irritated.
He said it as if he couldn't put up with this any longer.
Then he walked up to the spot in question.
"If nothing happens, I'm going home."
With that, he climbed over the surrounding fence and went inside.
All the other teachers warned him, but Mr. Iida just laughed and wouldn't listen.
"Ha ha, there's nothing here.
There's no way ghosts exist.
A bunch of grown adults, every last one of you..."
But just as he said that and started to climb back out over the fence...
Clouds covered the sun, and it grew a little dark.
Like a summer evening shower was coming.
And at that moment, he stopped moving.{p}
rows.08:b0d0: When the sun was completely hidden by clouds, they could faintly see shadows shaped like human hands around his legs. What do you think the other teachers did then?
rows.08:b20c:
He wasn't even making words anymore.
Mr. Iida was sinking before their very eyes.
By the time the priest came rushing over, only his head was left above the ground, and he had passed out.
rows.08:b2bc:
The priest immediately began chanting a sutra.
The other teachers took up their prayer beads and pressed their hands together, too.
Then Mr. Iida stopped sinking.
The priest began a full-scale exorcism.
And when the exorcism was over, he said this.
"Someone, bring a shovel."{p}
rows.08:b3c0:
The priest took the shovel and started digging Mr. Iida out.
The other teachers, who had been staring in a daze for a while, went to get shovels too and joined in. It took quite a long time to dig him all the way out.
When they finally got him out, Mr. Iida came to.
His body was covered in countless bite marks, and in places chunks had been bitten clean off.
Soon an ambulance was called, and Mr. Iida was taken away.{p}
rows.08:b558:
After that, he was in the hospital for quite a long time, but I hear he's out now and still teaching at another school.
Maybe the exorcism worked, because they say nothing happens there now.
I wonder what that earthbound spirit really is.
They say the bite marks on him back then were about the size of a child's.
Why a child's bite marks? I don't know.
If you want to know, you'll have to look into those school records I mentioned.
They say the records are kept in the safe in the principal's office.
Well, that's the end of my story.
Who's next?{p}
rows.08:b8d0:
After that, the priest arrived and performed the exorcism.
They dug the spot up right away, but there was nothing there.
According to the priest, it was a very powerful spirit, and he couldn't exorcise it completely.
But he was able to seal it, so nothing has happened since.
They say a few students at this school run away from home every year.
Maybe the seal has worn off at some point, and some of them have been swallowed by that ground.
Where is it, you ask? I don't know either.
All I've heard is that it's near the gym.
That's why, whenever I go to the gym, I make sure to walk only where I always walk.
{a}{f:,|,} please be careful too.
Well, that's the end of my story.
Who's next?{p}
rows.08:bb6c:
That's right. Good guess.
Normally, nobody in Japan would call one in.
But that's exactly what they did.
There was actually a reason they called in a Catholic priest.
The reason was that, supposedly, someone had once performed a ritual there to summon a demon.
The school must have had quite accurate information.
Maybe the exorcism worked, because that uncanny spirit has been gone ever since.
I don't know whether Western religion has any notion of an earthbound spirit.
But I think it's true that something was there.
Even if they call it something else, there must have been what we in Japan call an earthbound spirit.
Well then, enough preamble. Shall I begin the scary story?{p}
rows.08:bdb8: What I'm about to tell you is the story of the ritual that caused this spirit to appear.{p}
rows.08:be04:
Back then, there was a bit of an occult craze at this school.
During breaks, people everywhere were talking about the occult and performing rituals.
At first, though, it was just for fun.
But with crazes like that, there are usually a few people who get carried away and go too far, aren't there?
As if they were competing to see who could be more extreme.{p}
rows.08:bf48:
Among them was a girl named Eri Sawada, who didn't stand out at anything else.
She'd known a lot about the occult since before the craze hit the school, so the moment it caught on, she became popular.
And the more attention she got, the more extreme the things people demanded of her became.
To live up to them, she gradually went beyond the level of games.
And one day, she finally crossed a line that should never be crossed.
It all started with a conversation like this.{p}
rows.08:c0f4:
Endo, one of her occult friends, came over to Sawada's desk and brought it up.
"Eri, what are we doing next?"
At that, a crowd gathered around her again.
Until the occult caught on, she'd been the kind of girl who kept quiet in the corner of the classroom, but riding this craze, she'd really started to take the lead.
"Let's see... How about we meet at school at night and summon a demon?"
"Isn't that dangerous?"
Sawada answered the worried Endo.
"It's fine. If we don't make any wishes, it'll just go back where it came from.
Unless it's an extremely powerful demon, we'll be okay."
"Well, if you say so, Eri, I guess it's okay."
"Then everyone, we meet at school at midnight next Sunday."
"Okay."
"Until then, split up and gather the materials."
And so they decided to summon a demon.{p}
rows.08:c550: Still, she felt a little uneasy.
rows.08:c580:
(Summoning a demon just for fun...
But I have to live up to everyone's expectations...)
When she got to the school, several classmates had already gathered.
"Eri, you're late!
We can't start without you, you know."
"Sorry, my mom just wouldn't go to sleep."
With that, they waited for the rest of the group.
After a while, a few more came, but some members still hadn't shown up.
"It's already time.
Let's start, Eri."
"You're right. Maybe they couldn't sneak out of their houses."
With that, only the members who had gathered went around behind the school.{p}
rows.08:c774:
"This spot should do."
"Okay, draw the magic circle."
The girls set about their preparations.
"All right, let's begin.
Everyone, get inside the magic circle."
Sawada took out a battered old book and began chanting the incantation.{p}
